rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should test a key design choice. Config_003 tests multimodal fusion (weighted) with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder, which isolates the impact of multimodal integration. This clarifies whether combining modalities improves performance compared to image-only baselines, addressing a core design decision.

Existing evidence shows config_003 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, weighted fusion) achieves 0.6776 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt RNA encoder (a different representation) while keeping image encoder and fusion method the same improves performance. It isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, without changing multiple factors simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (config_003) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with a more complex model (imagenet_vit_l) while keeping the RNA encoder and other settings identical. This isolates the impact of image encoder complexity on performance, addressing uncertainty about whether more sophisticated encoders improve results without changing other critical components.

The existing evidence shows that using ImageNet ViT-L as the image encoder (config_019) outperforms ResNet50 (config_003). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping ViT-L and scvi_n200) improves performance, isolating the impact of aggregation method. This is critical for understanding if more complex aggregation mechanisms benefit the model, balancing exploration of key design choices with exploitation of proven components.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation achieves high accuracy (config_049: 0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing scvi_n200 RNA encoder with pca_n2000 (a simpler, lower-dimensional representation) maintains performance while isolating the impact of RNA encoding choices. It directly compares two RNA encoders under the same aggregation and fusion settings, addressing uncertainty about whether more complex encoders are necessary.

Existing evidence shows that using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion with imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_049) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to resnet50 image encoder while keeping transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (same as config_049) affects performance. It isolates the impact of image encoder choice, a critical design decision, to determine if imagenet_vit_l's superiority is consistent or if resnet50 could be a simpler alternative with comparable performance.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (config_049, 0.725) is the top performer. This experiment tests the effect of switching fusion type from weighted to concat while keeping RNA encoder (scvi_n200), image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), and aggregation (transformer) consistent. It isolates the impact of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, and clarifies whether concat fusion could be a viable alternative. This addresses uncertainty about the optimal fusion method while building on the strong foundation of the current top configuration.

Existing evidence shows that using ImageNet ViT L image encoder and scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_049) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests avgpool aggregation and concat fusion with the same encoders, isolating the impact of aggregation and fusion choices. It clarifies whether these factors are critical for performance, balancing exploration of key design decisions while building on prior successes.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder and transformer aggregation achieves high accuracy (config_049: 0.725). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt (while keeping image encoder, aggregation, and fusion consistent) improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA representation. It balances exploitation of strong image encoder/transformer aggregation combinations with exploration of RNA encoder choices.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests if using pca_n2000 RNA with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (changes in RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion) can improve performance, isolating the impact of these design choices. It balances exploration of RNA encoder alternatives while leveraging prior success with imagenet_vit_l and transformer aggregation.
